the phenomenological theories of superconductivity, based on the two uid model and the London theory, can be derived from the results of Marginal Fermi-Liquid (MFL) theory, which describes the strongly correlated superconductor in terms of a phenomenological model, and that the results of our calculations agree with the experimental data.

we have successfully applied the Marginal Fermi liquid model to the phenomenological two-uid model of the Gorter Casimir to calculate the critical eld in the type-I superconducting system, and also to the London theory to obtain the temperature dependence of magnetic eld penetration.

the phenomenological theories of superconductivity and their applications to strongly correlated superconducting materials.
the phenomenology of the superconductivity of the strongly correlated materials, based on the marginal Fermi liquid model.
the study of the electronic and magnetic properties of strongly correlated electron systems.

the phenomenology based Marginal Fermi liquid model is a very good approximation to the strongly correlated high temperature superconductors of the Cuprate type.
the Marginal Fermi Liqud model is a very good model in describing the properties of superconductivity.

the phenomenology based Marginal Fermi liquid theory provides a good description of the strongly correlated cuprates.
